topic.title: Creating, Compiling, and Executing a Java Program
topic.description: Steps to write, compile, and run Java programs
topic.chapter_title: Introduction to Computers, Programs, and Java

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered how your Java code turns into a running program? Let's break it down step by step!

• How to write your first Java program
• The magic of compiling Java code
• How to run your program and see results

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're writing a recipe (your Java code). Before you can cook it:
1⃣ You write the recipe in English (Java source code)
2⃣ A translator converts it to universal cooking instructions (bytecode)
3⃣ A chef (JVM) reads those instructions and makes your dish!

Java works the same way:
• Your Java code is like a recipe written in human-readable language
• The compiler translates it to bytecode - a universal format
• The JVM (Java Virtual Machine) executes this bytecode on any device

This is why Java is 'write once, run anywhere' - the bytecode works on any device with a JVM!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: javac compiles .java source files into .class bytecode files
The java command launches the JVM to execute the compiled bytecode
Bytecode is platform-independent and runs on any system with a compatible JVM
The classpath tells the JVM where to find compiled class files
Compilation errors must be fixed before the program can be executed

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Write → Compile → Run is the Java workflow. javac compiles .java to .class (bytecode) java command runs the bytecode on JVM. Practice with simple programs to master the process.
